blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution does not fix the specific number of members of the Election Commission.
The President of India determines the strength and composition of the Election Commission.
The Commission was originally a single-member body, but has functioned as a multi-member body since 1989.
In the multi-member setup, decisions are taken by majority vote among the members.
The President (not Parliament) holds the power to determine the number of Election Commissioners.
1989 is a frequently tested year when the Election Commission converted from a single-member body to a multi-member body.
Decisions in the Election Commission are not dictated by the Chief alone, but are decided by a majority vote.
